newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Hospitals full as Tajik typhoid outbreak spreads.
newsitem.headline: Hospitals full as Tajik typhoid outbreak spreads.

text.p: An outbreak of typhoid fever in the troubled Central Asian state of Tajikistan has spread beyond the capital Dushanbe and the city's hospitals can no longer cope with new cases, foreign aid officials said on Friday.

The regional delegation of the Geneva-based International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said 150 to 250 people were going down with the disease every day and it had spread to the southern city of Kulyab and the aluminium producing town of Tursunzade, west of Dushanbe.

The agency's Central Asian regional headquarters in the Kazakh capital Almaty said hospitals in Dushanbe were now full to capacity with 3,050 patients and that people falling sick with the disease had no choice but to remain at home.
On Thursday, the agency reported at least 10 deaths from typhoid in Tajikistan, which borders Afghanistan and China.
One aid worker based in the region said: "The next month is critical as even if emergency measures are implemented, there's a time lag of a month before they're effective."
He said tens of thousands could be affected.

Tajikistan, torn by four years of civil war, is one of the poorest republics of the former Soviet Union. Many of its 5.7 million people live in inadequate sanitary conditions, leading to outbreaks of infectious diseases.
Aid officials estimate Dushanbe's water system alone requires $10 to 15 million in repairs.
The IFRC has started distributing food and soap to Dushanbe hospitals and has given three tonnes of chlorine to the municipal authorities to clean up the city's water supply.
